metadata.system_title: Smart Honey Hive Tracking & Production Analytics
metadata.dataset_source: FAOSTAT (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations)
metadata.safety_disclaimer: HiveIQ is an exploratory screening and trend-estimation system developed for academic demonstration. Predictions represent statistical baseline estimates and must not replace professional on-site apiary inspections or official agricultural census audits.

logistic_regression.task: Honey Production Growth vs. Decline/Stable Classification

0.description: Countries with modest or developing honey yields (<15,000 tonnes/year), often serving local subsistence or specialty beekeeping.
0.actionable_advice: Prioritize localized hive health monitoring, basic disease prevention, and collective cooperative harvesting.

1.description: Countries with well-established commercial apiary sectors (20,000 to 100,000 tonnes/year) catering to domestic and export demands.
1.actionable_advice: Maintain proactive swarm control, floral corridor tracking, and seasonal weather risk mitigation.

2.description: Global industrial market leaders (>300,000 tonnes/year) with high hive density and mechanized processing facilities.
2.actionable_advice: Focus on national biodiversity preservation, pesticide buffer zones, and macro export quality verification.

inspection_alerts.temp_cold: Temperature below 32°C: Risk of brood chilling and slowed wax secretion. Check hive insulation.
inspection_alerts.temp_hot: Temperature above 36.5°C: Risk of overheating and honey softening. Ensure hive ventilation and shaded cover.
inspection_alerts.humidity_high: Humidity exceeds 68%: Moisture buildup creates high susceptibility to chalkbrood and nosema.
inspection_alerts.pests_varroa: Varroa destructor suspected: Implement immediate non-chemical screening or oxalic acid vapor according to seasonal threshold.
